title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1LC0LE_1RA0LB_1RB---_0LF0RC_0RA1LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1LC0LE_1RA0LB_1RB---_0LF0RC_0RA1LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is a few long alternating blocks (10)^n separated by single 1s. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps; an exact macro simulator (blocks of 16 cells) finds no halt in the first 1012 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,565 cells have been visited and 1,782 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.335). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.335).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>12</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact macro simulator (blocks of 16 cells) runs 1012 steps without a halt. The macro simulator cuts the tape into blocks of K cells, run-length codes them, and crosses a whole run at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with; it agrees with the plain simulator tools/c/tmrun cell for cell.

claims.title: Alternating blocks halved and merged
claims.text: At the moments the head reaches a new cell between steps 9.66·107 and 9.91·107, the tape is a chain of (10)^n blocks: 610 split into 306 and 305, 202 cut to 102 while its neighbour grew from 305 to 406, down to a single block of 820.

claims.title: The halting state, seen from the run
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps state D was entered 106,974 times, always reading a 0 (D1 halts).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Its tape is a chain of long alternating blocks separated by single 1s; blocks are halved, one half merging into the next block, until one block is left, and then it is split again.

facts.text: No halt in an exact macro simulator (blocks of 16 cells).
Alternating blocks are halved and merged until one is left.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the C simulator; 3,565 cells visited.

sections.heading: What the machine does
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell. With a for 10, around step 9.7·107:

• step 96,586,116: C>0 a 0 a^610 0^2 1 a^202 1 (left end)
  • step 97,150,995: F>0^2 a^306 0^2 1 a^305 1 a^202 1 (left end)
  • step 97,437,314: 1 a^308 1 a^305 1 a^202 1 A>0 (right end)
  • step 97,500,752: 1 a^308 1 a^406 0 a^102 1 A>0 (right end)
  • step 97,534,323: C>0 a 0 a^307 0^2 a^509 1 (left end)
  • step 97,681,430: 0 a^154 0 a^664 1 A>0 (right end)
  • step 99,010,412: C>0 a^820 1 (left end)
  • step 99,015,341: C>0 a 0 a^819 0^2 1 (left end)

A block of 610 copies of 10 is split into 306 and 305; the last block shrinks from 202 to 102 while the block before it grows from 305 to 406; the remainder is merged (406 + 102 to 509); then the first block is halved (308 to 154, the block after it growing to 664); and at step 99,010,412 the chain is a single block of 820, which is split again. Halving a block costs many passes over it, so the width grows much more slowly than the step count: after 108 steps 1,644 cells have been visited.

This resembles the solid-block chains of 1RB1LA_1LA0RC_1RD1RC_1LE0RC_---0LF_1LE0LA and 1RB1LA_1LC0RA_0LF0LD_1RE1LD_1RE0RB_---0LC, with alternating blocks instead; the exact rules have not been worked out.

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The halting transition is D reading a 1. D is entered only from A reading a 1 (1RD), so a halt needs A>1 1. In the first 108 steps D was entered 106,974 times, every time on a 0, and 105,807 of those times at least 7 cells from the left end.
Whether A ever stands on 1 1 is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.335). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.335).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,565 cells (1,269 left of the start, 1,617 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: chain of alternating blocks, halved and merged
